requirements.requirement: Provide a dedicated uploader identity and SSH key on node2 that targets a separate ingest application identity on node1.
requirements.summary: A locked, non-administrative uploader account with a dedicated ED25519 key was created on node2. Its SSH client profile targets the distinct ingest account on node1, whose authorized key invokes the receiver.

requirements.requirement: Prevent the ingest key from running arbitrary commands, obtaining a shell or PTY, or establishing forwarding.
requirements.summary: An attempted remote touch command was replaced by the forced receiver and did not create its marker; the supplied stdin was stored instead. Remote forwarding was behaviorally rejected. Effective SSH policy also disables PTY, forwarding, tunneling, agent/X11 forwarding, user RC files, and password authentication.

requirements.requirement: Store each submitted newline-delimited batch as a separate file under the specified received directory, preserving submitted bytes.
requirements.summary: The sample submission produced a uniquely named receipt in the required directory with identical size, SHA-256, and byte-for-byte comparison. Additional submissions produced distinct receipts, including successful end-to-end submissions after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the existing receipt and sample batch.
requirements.summary: The final post-restart observations retain the original sample and prior receipt with the same hashes recorded in the preparation baseline; the first uploaded sample receipt also remains intact.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on AlmaLinux 9.6 with kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6 before and after execution. The implementation used the platform's installed OpenSSH and standard shell utilities, and final package-health checks passed.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral and final-state evidence. The dedicated key successfully performs exact-byte ingestion while arbitrary command execution and forwarding are blocked; seeded data, OS release, kernel, and functionality survive verified restarts of both nodes. The only hygiene defect is one abandoned temporary restriction-test file on node2.
limitations: No explicit interactive shell/PTY attempt was captured; shell denial is supported by the directly demonstrated forced-command boundary and effective PermitTTY=no policy.

Lifecycle file and socket inventories are bounded rather than exhaustive, though they directly identify the lone test-file residue and show no failed services, unexpected listeners, or package inconsistency.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Chronological review found no unnecessary state-changing experiments: account/key creation, receiver and SSH configuration, test submissions, marker setup, and restarts all had clear task or evidence roles. One executor-caused residue remained on node2: /tmp/restriction-test.ndjson, created for the restriction test and not cleaned afterward. No failed services, added listeners, or package damage were observed. Both nodes completed the restart protocol with healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service, data, and end-to-end ingestion.
